messages:
maya.k: Hey team — planning to spend May–Jul in Denver, will this be 'temporary hub' or do I need to change homebase? Any impact on the WFH stipend & payroll tax?

devon: @maya.k If it's under 90 days usually temporary hub, no change to homebase. But taxes can get weird, pinging @lina (People Ops).

lina (People Ops): @maya.k quick clarifying q: will you be working remotely full-time or splitting with a coworking location there?

maya.k: Full remote, but I'll be desk booking at a partner coworking 2–3 days/wk. Not moving company furniture or filing any residency docs.

jordan_p: In that case we treat it as transient remote. Stipend proration applies if you change homebase mid-month. For 3 full months, stipend continues the same if homebase stays the same.

lina (People Ops): Yep — policy: temporary stays < 6 months don't change homebase. WFH allowance continues; no automatic proration unless you formally update homebase in HRIS. If you want the stipend pro-rated for partial months we can do that manually.

maya.k: Good to know. Any tax nexus risk for Redwood or me as an employee? :thinking: 

taxbot: FYI — short stays <183 days usually don't create employer nexus, but local payroll/withholding rules differ by state. Recommend notifying payroll & tax for assessment.

sam (Payroll): @maya.k can you fill this form? https://intranet.redwood/company/remote-declare — tick 'temporary hub' and add dates. We'll run a nexus check and confirm withholding. If withholding changes we'll notify you before any payroll adjustment.

maya.k: Done, form submitted. Thanks all.

lina (People Ops): Thanks! We'll loop in US tax to confirm. If there's any change to withholding or benefits eligibility we'll message you here. :wave:

devon: tagging for records: @people-ops we should add a short note to the policy doc about coworking-days guidance — seen a few similar asks.

lina (People Ops): Agreed — filing a docs update ticket after tax confirmation. :thumbsup:
